title: Stop losing held chat on a Remote Claude and make reconnect drivable
body:
Context: commits bdf3877 and 54648b5 (read both bodies), docs/remote-sessions.md, docs/agent-state.md, spec docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-20-remote-sessions-design.md (The way back, Agent state, Results). Foreman delivers chat by pasting into the agent's pane and sending Enter after ready::SUBMIT_DELAY; that only works when the agent sits at its input box. 54648b5 added a chat hold for a hooked Remote Claude (ReadyGate::hold, remote::ChatHold, remote::chat_hold, remote::note_route, claude_with_hooks, prompt_index).
THE HUMAN'S REQUIREMENT, verbatim intent: a clean production-ready implementation that is PROVEN working. Reproduce each defect first by driving the real application, record the outcome, fix it, then drive the real application again and record that the defect is gone. A unit test alone proves nothing here. If you cannot reproduce a defect, say so with the runs you made and do not invent a fix for it.
How to drive the real application. Test Remote: andy@192.168.8.168 (hostname Falador, Debian, key login; never ask for a password; Claude Code and Codex installed, Grok not). You run inside the INSTALLED foreman, which lacks these changes; never stop any foreman by name and never touch an instance you did not start. Build your own: cargo build --release --target-dir target/agent/hooks. Config dir target/agent/appdata-s2hp4s already holds settings.json (Remote named falador) and a workspace.json with one empty Project; reuse it. Launch with APPDATA pointed there and the environment stripped the way scripts/run-dev.ps1 does; drive it through ITS pipe (foreman-ctl-<pid>-*, listed from PowerShell with Get-ChildItem \\.\pipe\), FOREMAN_PIPE set, FOREMAN_PROJECT_ID / FOREMAN_TERMINAL_ID unset, the exe you built as the CLI. Each attempt uses a NEW never-trusted directory under /tmp on the Remote. Never kill a process on the Remote you did not start. At the end: close your Sessions, stop YOUR instances by PID, remove your /tmp directories and their Claude transcripts, and remove only your own trust entries from the Remote's ~/.claude.json (verify the file round-trips before writing; otherwise list them).
Recording. Write a run log as you go (scratch file, not the repo): one line per run with wall-clock time, what you launched, what you did, and the observed outcome (snapshot text, status --json, room history, the agent's transcript on the Remote where that is the only proof a paste arrived). Summarise it as BEFORE and AFTER tables (runs, failures) in the commit body and in a new Results entry in the spec. Never print a token in the repo.
Hard rules: nothing may assume foreman, its skills or hook files exist on the Remote; a Remote agent may post chat, read history, read status and report hook events and nothing else; requests without any new field stay byte-identical on the wire, with a compat test; nothing under cfg(test) spawns a process or opens a socket outside the remote_probe network guard; do not detect agent state from screen text (see foreman-agent-state-campaign); do not launch Codex with its hook-trust bypass flag; do not mark anything on Grok or a Windows Remote as tested.

THIS CARD: held input is lost when the hold opens on SessionStart, and reconnect cannot be proven.
Defect. ChatHold::UntilStart releases on Claude's SessionStart, which fires about 0.3 s after the trust dialog is answered while the REPL is still mounting; a paste at that moment can vanish (54648b5's worker saw 1 loss in 3). UntilStart is used for a bare claude, a reconnect (claude --continue), a one-word brief (prompt_index refuses it although UserPromptSubmit follows), and a launch by path (claude_with_hooks matches the file stem, prompt_index wants the bare name). On reconnect the lost text is the new reply note: the agent keeps the dead token and its posts get 401, and foreman believes the note was delivered.
Step 0, a way to drive reconnect. No CLI verb can press Enter on the disconnect bar, so reconnect has never been shown live. Add a LOCAL control-plane verb `foreman reconnect <terminal>` that does exactly what Enter on the disconnect bar does for a disconnected Remote Session and refuses anything else (not a Remote Session, not disconnected). It is a new request kind: existing requests stay byte-identical, add the compat test, document it in the CLI help and in docs/remote-sessions.md, and make sure the Tunnel cannot reach it (a Remote agent must not be able to reconnect panes; test that). To disconnect a Session for a test, kill its ssh child on this PC by PID, or the agent's sshd session on the Remote if it is yours.
Step 1, reproduce BEFORE any fix, on today's main, at least 10 runs each, recording losses:
 R1 bare claude in a never-trusted directory; post a broadcast while the dialog shows; answer the dialog with send; did the post reach Claude (transcript on the Remote)?
 R2 claude "<multi-word brief>" as the control (expected 0 losses).
 R3 one-word brief, same procedure.
 R4 launch by path (the Remote's `command -v claude` result) with a multi-word brief.
 R5 reconnect: open a Claude that has done one turn, kill its ssh, `foreman reconnect`, then ask it in the room to post back; does it use the NEW token (post arrives) or the old one (nothing arrives; check for 401 with a manual curl if useful)?
Step 2, fix. The human has left the design to you; requirements: no held input is ever lost or duplicated, order is kept, and nothing reaches the trust dialog. Decide from measurement, not guesswork: measure, over at least 20 launches, how long after SessionStart Claude's input box accepts a paste. Acceptable shapes: release UntilStart a measured, justified interval after SessionStart (state the measured distribution and the margin in a comment and the docs; this is NOT the blind timer that was rejected, because the hook has already proven the dialog is past), or a better signal if you find one that is not screen-text detection. One-word briefs and path launches whose UserPromptSubmit will follow should wait for UserPromptSubmit like any brief; fix the predicates so the hold choice and the hooks choice cannot disagree (one pure function with a table test), without loosening which argument prompt_index is willing to REWRITE. If a slash-command brief (starts with /) fires no UserPromptSubmit, find out on the Remote and handle it.
Step 3, verify AFTER, same procedures R1 to R5, at least 20 runs each for R1, R3, R5 and 10 for R2, R4. Target: 0 losses. If any loss remains, do not land it as fixed: report the numbers and block the card.
Done when:
- `foreman reconnect` exists, is local-only, refused for anything but a disconnected Remote Session, with compat and Tunnel-refusal tests
- BEFORE and AFTER tables for R1 to R5 are in the commit body and the spec's Results, with AFTER at 0 losses, or the card is blocked with the numbers
- the hold/hooks choice is one pure function with a table test; unit tests pin order, no loss, no duplicate across the release
- docs/remote-sessions.md, docs/agent-state.md and both providers' foreman-dispatch skill copies (embedded-skill rebuild rule in foreman-docs-and-writing) say what is true; cite-guard clean; full suite passes
Gate: cargo test --target-dir target/agent; pwsh -File .claude/hooks/cite-guard.ps1 -All
